$comment: Normative vectors for docs/design/portable-query-payload.md, checked by eng/check-portable-query-payload-vectors.cs. encode: intent -> canonical bytes, which must also decode and re-emit unchanged. encode-reject: intent refused before canonicalizing, with reason. reject: bytes refused at decode, with reason. pair: two (queryId, canonical) states and whether they are the same query. Keys, dimensions, and named orders are illustrative.

encode.name: package-query
encode.description: A package query: three terms including the typed prefix, one execution bound, no stages, no order. Scope travels as a term; its value is the typed prefix, not the host spelling with its terminal star.

encode.name: package-query-entered-in-another-order
encode.description: The same query with terms and properties supplied in a different sequence. Identical bytes to package-query: both share one link and one packet state.

encode.name: package-query-with-exact-duplicate
encode.description: An exact duplicate term collapses because conjunction is idempotent; bytes equal package-query. The four parsed terms were still charged against the term limit before collapse.

encode.name: bounds-entered-in-another-order
encode.description: Two bounds supplied in the opposite sequence sort by dimension; declaration sequence carries no meaning between independent dimensions.

encode.name: all-four-parts
encode.description: Every part present once, showing property order t, b, s, o and a field-list baseline order.

encode.name: row-query-baseline-and-ranking
encode.description: Rows of at least medium confidence, baseline by name, first twenty, then the five worst by triage. The ranking operation names stage index 1, the top.

encode.name: row-query-reversed-pipeline
encode.description: The same parts with the stage pipeline reversed: a different question, so different bytes whether or not a given input distinguishes the results.

encode.name: order-operations-supplied-out-of-role-order
encode.description: Operations supplied ranking-first canonicalize to base first then ascending stage index; outer sequence carries nothing once each operation names its role.

encode.name: operation-boundary-a
encode.description: Baseline [a asc], ranking [b desc, c asc]. Must not share bytes with operation-boundary-b: each operation array is its own boundary.

encode.name: operation-boundary-b
encode.description: Baseline [a asc, b desc], ranking [c asc]. Same field terms as operation-boundary-a divided differently; different bytes.

encode.name: field-sequence-a
encode.description: A field-list operation ordering by a then b. Field terms compose lexicographically, so their sequence is meaning and is preserved.

encode.name: field-sequence-b
encode.description: The same two field terms, b then a. A different order, so different bytes from field-sequence-a.

encode.name: window-with-open-bounds
encode.description: Window keeps three slots with null for an omitted bound: a gap in place, never a shorter tuple.

encode.name: scalar-order-not-utf16-order
encode.description: Keys U+E000 and U+10000. Scalar (UTF-8 byte) order places U+E000 first; UTF-16 code-unit order would place U+10000 first. The bytes follow scalar order.

encode.name: quotes-backslash-and-short-escapes
encode.description: Quote, backslash, and the five C0 controls with short escapes round-trip in their short forms.

encode.name: c0-control-lowercase-hex
encode.description: A C0 control without a short escape emits as lowercase u00xx, the packet owner's spelling. System.Text.Json's encoders emit uppercase here.

encode.name: raw-scalars-above-ascii
encode.description: U+007F, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029, e-acute, and an emoji all emit as raw UTF-8. System.Text.Json's encoders escape every one of these.

encode.name: literal-backslash-u-text
encode.description: A value whose text is the six characters backslash u d 8 0 0. It is ordinary text, escapes its backslash, and is not an unpaired surrogate.

encode.name: joint-maximum
encode.description: The admissible payload with the most JSON values: 24 terms, 8 bounds, seven top stages plus one window, one eight-field baseline plus seven named rankings. 204 values, far under 3 KiB, so here the value count binds before the byte count.

encode.name: identity-at-maximum
encode.description: A 64-byte key and a 64-byte dimension: each exact identity maximum is admissible.

encode.name: value-at-maximum
encode.description: A 256-byte value: the exact value maximum is admissible.

encode.name: count-at-maximum
encode.description: A count of 2147483647, the top of the Count domain, is admissible as a bound maximum and as a stage count.

encode.name: window-equal-bounds
encode.description: A closed window whose start equals its end selects one row and is ordered.

encode.name: payload-near-byte-maximum
encode.description: Twenty-four terms with 99-byte values and eight bounds: a term-heavy payload close to the 3 KiB limit, showing the byte count binding before the part counts.

encode-reject.name: too-many-terms-as-parsed
encode-reject.description: Twenty-five identical terms would collapse to one, but limits are charged as parsed: the intent is refused on the twenty-fifth. Collapse can never buy unbounded parse work.

encode-reject.name: repeated-dimension-in-intent
encode-reject.description: Two bounds on one dimension are refused at intent construction, before any encoding.

encode-reject.name: nine-bounds
encode-reject.description: Nine bounds exceed the limit of eight.

encode-reject.name: nine-stages
encode-reject.description: Nine stages exceed the limit of eight.

encode-reject.name: nine-order-operations
encode-reject.description: Nine operations exceed the limit of eight, even with stages to bind to.

encode-reject.name: identity-one-over
encode-reject.description: A 65-byte key exceeds the identity limit.

encode-reject.name: value-one-over-in-intent
encode-reject.description: A 257-byte value is refused on the intent side too.

encode-reject.name: nine-field-terms-in-intent
encode-reject.description: Nine field terms across operations exceed the aggregate on the intent side too.

encode-reject.name: payload-too-large-as-intent
encode-reject.description: Twenty-four distinct terms with 128-byte values: every part and every text within its limit, yet the canonical form exceeds 3 KiB. The byte limit is charged on the canonical form before emission succeeds.

encode-reject.name: window-unordered-in-intent
encode-reject.description: A closed window whose end precedes its start cannot construct a selection stage; the stage owner's precondition is enforced at construction.

encode-reject.name: count-over-domain-in-intent
encode-reject.description: 2147483648 is outside the Count domain, however it is spelled.

reject.name: pretty-printed
reject.description: Whitespace between tokens is not canonical.

reject.name: terms-unsorted
reject.description: Terms out of scalar order are not canonical bytes.

reject.name: bounds-unsorted
reject.description: Bounds out of dimension order are not canonical bytes.

reject.name: properties-out-of-order
reject.description: Property order is exactly t, b, s, o.

reject.name: exact-duplicate-terms-on-the-wire
reject.description: Canonical form has already collapsed exact duplicates.

reject.name: order-operations-out-of-role-order-on-the-wire
reject.description: Operations emit base first then ascending stage index.

reject.name: escaped-ascii
reject.description: An escaped ASCII letter decodes to the same value as the raw letter but is not the canonical spelling.

reject.name: uppercase-c0-hex
reject.description: An uppercase hex escape for a C0 control is the System.Text.Json spelling, not the packet's.

reject.name: escaped-non-ascii
reject.description: An escaped non-ASCII scalar is not canonical; the packet emits it raw.

reject.name: surrogate-pair-escape
reject.description: An emoji as a surrogate-pair escape decodes correctly but is not canonical; the packet emits four raw bytes.

reject.name: empty-part-emitted
reject.description: An absent or empty part is omitted, never emitted as an empty array.

reject.name: unknown-property
reject.description: The object is closed.

reject.name: duplicate-property
reject.description: A repeated property is invalid.

reject.name: not-an-object
reject.description: The payload is one object, never an array or scalar.

reject.name: malformed
reject.description: Text that is not JSON is refused before any shape rule applies.

reject.name: repeated-bound-dimension-different-maxima
reject.description: One dimension carries at most one bound; two maxima are a contradiction, not a narrower request.

reject.name: repeated-bound-dimension-identical
reject.description: Even identical duplicates are refused rather than collapsed; a second bound has no meaning to preserve.

reject.name: unknown-operator
reject.description: Only eq, ne, gte, lte. There is no strict lt or gt.

reject.name: unknown-stage
reject.description: Stage tokens are fixed.

reject.name: unknown-direction
reject.description: Direction tokens are fixed.

reject.name: unknown-order-kind
reject.description: Order kinds are named or fields.

reject.name: unknown-role-string
reject.description: The only string role is base.

reject.name: head-with-null
reject.description: null is permitted only in the two window bound slots.

reject.name: null-identity
reject.description: null is not an identity.

reject.name: window-wrong-arity
reject.description: Window is always three slots; an omitted bound is null, not a shorter tuple.

reject.name: term-wrong-arity
reject.description: A term is exactly three slots.

reject.name: bound-wrong-arity
reject.description: A bound is exactly two slots.

reject.name: named-order-wrong-arity
reject.description: A named operation is role, kind, reference, direction.

reject.name: fields-order-odd-terms
reject.description: A field-list operation pairs every key with a direction.

reject.name: fields-order-no-terms
reject.description: A field-list operation carries at least one pair.

reject.name: role-names-a-non-top-stage
reject.description: A ranking role must name a top stage.

reject.name: role-out-of-range
reject.description: A ranking role must index an existing stage.

reject.name: duplicate-base
reject.description: At most one operation carries base.

reject.name: duplicate-stage-role
reject.description: At most one operation per ranking stage.

reject.name: bound-maximum-not-integer
reject.description: Maxima are JSON integers.

reject.name: bound-maximum-negative
reject.description: Counts are positive and unsigned.

reject.name: bound-maximum-zero
reject.description: Counts are positive.

reject.name: count-with-leading-zero
reject.description: A leading zero is not JSON at all.

reject.name: count-with-exponent
reject.description: No exponent form.

reject.name: count-over-domain
reject.description: 2147483648 is outside the Count domain.

reject.name: count-beyond-int64
reject.description: A count wider than any host integer is not a Count; the domain, not a host type, decides.

reject.name: window-unordered
reject.description: A closed window whose end precedes its start is refused at decode, before it can reach a resolver.

reject.name: nine-bounds-on-the-wire
reject.description: Nine bounds exceed the limit on the wire side too.

reject.name: nine-stages-on-the-wire
reject.description: Nine stages exceed the limit on the wire side too.

reject.name: nine-order-operations-on-the-wire
reject.description: Nine operations exceed the limit on the wire side too.

reject.name: too-many-terms
reject.description: Twenty-five terms exceed the limit of 24.

reject.name: too-many-order-field-terms
reject.description: Nine field terms across operations exceed the eight-term aggregate.

reject.name: value-too-long
reject.description: A 257-byte value exceeds the 256-byte limit.

reject.name: identity-too-long
reject.description: A 65-byte dimension exceeds the 64-byte identity limit.

reject.name: payload-too-large
reject.description: Twenty-four terms with 128-byte values: every part within its count and every text within its length, yet over 3 KiB. The byte limit binds.

reject.name: unpaired-high-surrogate
reject.description: A lone high surrogate escape is refused, never repaired to U+FFFD.

reject.name: unpaired-low-surrogate
reject.description: A lone low surrogate escape is refused.

pair.name: same-bytes-two-vocabularies
pair.description: Identical payload bytes under two vocabularies are two different queries; the keys resolve against different namespaces.

pair.name: same-query-two-entries
pair.description: The same query entered in two orders is one query: same vocabulary, same canonical bytes.
